sentences.text: Researchers used animal models to investigate how manipulating SIRT6 levels in excitatory neurons affected stress responses. Forcing these neurons to produce more SIRT6 reduced stress-induced sadness and anxiety, while removing the protein caused depression-like behaviors even without stress. Additionally, a specific hippocampal neuron type that disappeared after stress returned when SIRT6 levels were raised.

Gene network analysis showed that the protein OVOL2 controls stress-related gene activity, and SIRT6 physically binds to OVOL2 to maintain its stability. This binding triggers the production of other proteins like Nrg1, and a drug activating SIRT6 produced the same stress-fighting effects observed with genetic changes.
The authors suggest that targeting SIRT6 could be a new way to treat depression based on these results.
